name: Alizarine Pink
lede: Alizarine Pink is a soft, warm pink from Ridgway's 1912 chart, one of the rarest colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A rare pink
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 plate XIII gives this pink the name Alizarine Pink, hue 1′, tone d, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files a close match in its block 2 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[jasper-pink]], [[mauvelous]], [[faded-pink]] and [[dusty-pink]], at 3.4, 3.5, 4, 3.5, 4 and 4 ΔE [1]. Among named pinks it sits near [[rose]] and [[pink]] itself [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Alizarine Pink in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, one of the rarer colors we track, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is a Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John the Baptist, from 1525, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. With so few matches, the data cannot support a reliable peak decade or painter; inside a painting it most often sits as a highlight, in 71 percent of its appearances [2].
